videos.script: Carreto had sixty-one rules on a wiki page, and nobody followed them. {{wiki}} The engineers were not careless. Nobody can remember sixty-one rules, and nothing told them when they broke one. {{forgotten}} In March, one forgotten rule cost three hundred and twelve drivers their Friday pay. A job in Payments reached inside another team's code, and that code changed. {{payout}} This lesson is about the few rules worth having. What separates a principle, a standard and a guideline. Why each standard needs a reason and an owner. {{nine}} Then it hands the checking to a machine. You will read a short Python program that fails the build when one team imports another team's internals. You will see it fail, and then pass. {{checker}} Last comes the part most standards skip. How to ask for an exception. How to tell whether a standard is really followed. And how to retire one whose reason has gone. {{retire}}
